name: Storm-1295
keyCapabilities: Multi-platform lateral movement and exploitation (Windows, Linux, macOS)
Sophisticated credential theft (LSASS harvesting, Kerberoasting, Session Hijacking)
recommendedActions: Implement phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO2/WebAuthn) to mitigate AitM and session theft.
Monitor for and block outgoing traffic on non-standard ports and domains showing pseudo-random patterns.
Restrict the use of LOLBins such as mshta.exe, regsvr32.exe, and bin_dir binaries used in lateral movement.
Implement aggressive monitoring/alerting for LSASS access and Kerberos ticket extraction (T1558).
Audit and monitor DNS queries for 'water torture' patterns or high-frequency rapid subdomain changes.
Conduct regular integrity checks on core system files and firmware to detect unauthorized modifications.
Monitor logs for common indicators of session hijacking, such as login attempts from disparate geographic locations using the same token.
Deploy EDR solutions capable of detecting PowerShell, Python, and JavaScript macro-based execution in unusual contexts.
Scan network environment for outbound connections to known PhaaS infrastructure markers.
Conduct targeted defense training focusing on identifying sophisticated phishing schemes targeting high-priority staff.
campaignsText: Storm-1295 exhibits a sophisticated, service-oriented operational model centered on the Greatness PhaaS platform since mid-2022. Their campaigns are characterized by high-technical maturity, moving beyond simple credential harvesting to complex session hijacking and infrastructure manipulation. They are observed targeting government and defense sectors globally (notably in the Middle East and North America), utilizing multi-step protocols for C2, such as Domain Fronting and usage of non-standard ports. Their operation shows a persistent focus on high-value targets including activists and embassy personnel.
description: Storm-1295 is an advanced threat actor specializing in the operation of the 'Greatness' phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platform. The group utilizes sophisticated Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) techniques and infrastructure manipulation to target high-value individuals in defense, government, and critical infrastructure sectors.
goals: Storm-1295's primary goal is financial gain through the provision of 'Phishing-as-a-Service' (PhaaS) and potentially intelligence gathering for higher-level objectives. Their targeting profile is highly specific, focusing on individuals in government, defense, energy, media, and non-profit organizations. They concentrate on geographically defined regions including the Middle East and North America, specifically aiming at high-ranking officials and activists to maximize the impact of their credential harvesting operations.
